key_insight: For TCM tongue diagnosis, the best results came from a parameter-efficient ConvNeXt-Tiny model paired with restrained color augmentation and weak-group ensembling, highlighting that training choices mattered as much as architecture.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests AI-assisted tongue image classification can become more reliable with careful model design, but it remains a research tool rather than a standalone clinical decision-maker.
method: Compared 6 backbones, 4 loss functions, 5 augmentation strategies, and 6 training strategies
Evaluated with rigorous 5-fold cross-validation on TongueDx2 and a merged larger dataset
evidence_signal: On TongueDx2 (5,109 images; 976 expert-annotated), the best model reached weighted-F1 0.6625, and on the merged 11,101-sample dataset performance rose to 0.7761.
watch_item: Results depend on dataset scale and label setup; expanding labels from 13 to 45 caused a major performance collapse, so implementation should match label granularity carefully.
paper_title: What Makes Deep Learning Work for Traditional Chinese Medicine Tongue Diagnosis? A Comprehensive Ablation Study
